input.summary:
Rear porch furnished in parts/room-30.mjs: two dark-oak table groups (stair chairs, fence-and-top-slab tables) with standing lanterns, a white rug, barrels with flower pots, and lamp posts either side of the lane from the rear door to the steps.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; the room check on a test copy with the porch floor, columns and steps added reads OK (75/82 floor cells reachable from the steps, min light 8, no dark or dim cells, fit OK, no refused writes, all blocks on palette).
The lane x46..49 from the door to the steps stays clear; nothing sits on the z79 column cells.
left: In this copy the colonnade (rearPorch) and the shell do not yet build the porch floor y3, the six z79 columns or the rear steps, so `mcd room` on the real build.nbt reports no way in and floating furniture. I verified in a test copy (/tmp/part37-check) with those added; re-run `mcd room` after the merge.
The walk from the rear door z75 (x47..48) depends on the living-room and kitchen rooms (parts 11/12), which are stubs here; only the steps side was tested.

plan.md has no per-room rows in its checklist and I did not edit its Notes, so nothing is ticked there. elements.md 'Lighting' is shared with P6 and the hall, so I left it unticked; the rear porch lamp posts and table lanterns are the part of it I built.
The lamp posts at x39, x46 and x49 on z79 and the lantern on the floor at (52,4,78) depend on the porch floor being present, otherwise they float.

waste.what: Checking the room needed a test copy: a script that lays the porch floor, the z79 columns and the rear steps into a copy of build.nbt, because this copy's stub colonnade builds none of them. The check was run on that copy by hand.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and one scratch script; the real build reported floating furniture and no way in
waste.tool: `mcd room --assume-floor "<box>"` or a `--with <part-stub-fill>` option; or `mcd room` should say 'no floor under the box' instead of reporting unreachable

waste.what: Drew the three furniture layers as literal 22-character rows and counted the columns by hand to keep them aligned on x37..58; also iterated the lamp-post and lantern positions after each light check.
waste.cost: about 4 rebuild and check cycles; 2 rewrites of the z79 rows
waste.tool: `mcd plan` could print the floor grid as a sparse coordinate list (x,z -> char) that layers() accepts; a `layers` option that takes {x,z,y,block} entries would remove the row arithmetic

waste.what: Looked up the lantern and chair state formats (lantern hanging as a string 'false', stairs facing) by reading the build library source.
waste.tool: `mcd states <block>` already exists; a note in the toolkit that layers() legend states must be strings would have saved the grep

companions.task: Lay the rear porch's own shell (smooth_quartz floor y3, slim quartz columns at z79, the three rear steps and their bricks) so the furnished room has a floor to stand on and a walkable way in from the lawn.
Review the two lamp posts either side of the rear steps and the floor lantern against the east chairs, to confirm the lane stays bright enough for the arrival at dusk.

structured_output.summary:
Rear porch furnished in parts/room-30.mjs: two dark-oak table groups (stair chairs, fence-and-top-slab tables) with standing lanterns, a white rug, barrels with flower pots, and lamp posts either side of the lane from the rear door to the steps.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; the room check on a test copy with the porch floor, columns and steps added reads OK (75/82 floor cells reachable from the steps, min light 8, no dark or dim cells, fit OK, no refused writes, all blocks on palette).
The lane x46..49 from the door to the steps stays clear; nothing sits on the z79 column cells.
left: In this copy the colonnade (rearPorch) and the shell do not yet build the porch floor y3, the six z79 columns or the rear steps, so `mcd room` on the real build.nbt reports no way in and floating furniture. I verified in a test copy (/tmp/part37-check) with those added; re-run `mcd room` after the merge.
The walk from the rear door z75 (x47..48) depends on the living-room and kitchen rooms (parts 11/12), which are stubs here; only the steps side was tested.

plan.md has no per-room rows in its checklist and I did not edit its Notes, so nothing is ticked there. elements.md 'Lighting' is shared with P6 and the hall, so I left it unticked; the rear porch lamp posts and table lanterns are the part of it I built.
The lamp posts at x39, x46 and x49 on z79 and the lantern on the floor at (52,4,78) depend on the porch floor being present, otherwise they float.

waste.what: Checking the room needed a test copy: a script that lays the porch floor, the z79 columns and the rear steps into a copy of build.nbt, because this copy's stub colonnade builds none of them. The check was run on that copy by hand.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and one scratch script; the real build reported floating furniture and no way in
waste.tool: `mcd room --assume-floor "<box>"` or a `--with <part-stub-fill>` option; or `mcd room` should say 'no floor under the box' instead of reporting unreachable

waste.what: Drew the three furniture layers as literal 22-character rows and counted the columns by hand to keep them aligned on x37..58; also iterated the lamp-post and lantern positions after each light check.
waste.cost: about 4 rebuild and check cycles; 2 rewrites of the z79 rows
waste.tool: `mcd plan` could print the floor grid as a sparse coordinate list (x,z -> char) that layers() accepts; a `layers` option that takes {x,z,y,block} entries would remove the row arithmetic

waste.what: Looked up the lantern and chair state formats (lantern hanging as a string 'false', stairs facing) by reading the build library source.
waste.tool: `mcd states <block>` already exists; a note in the toolkit that layers() legend states must be strings would have saved the grep

companions.task: Lay the rear porch's own shell (smooth_quartz floor y3, slim quartz columns at z79, the three rear steps and their bricks) so the furnished room has a floor to stand on and a walkable way in from the lawn.
Review the two lamp posts either side of the rear steps and the floor lantern against the east chairs, to confirm the lane stays bright enough for the arrival at dusk.
